body.translated_text: <s>Piṇḍīkrama</s> (The Stage of Aggregation)
Composed by <s>Ācārya Nāgārjuna</s>
<s>Piṇḍīkrama</s> (The Stage of Aggregation)
Homage to the Omniscient One

children.translated_text: Free from the conduct of the three worlds, equal to space, the self-nature of all existences,

children.text: śuddhaṃ śāntaṃ viviktaṃ paramaśivamayaṃ yogināmeva gamyam |
children.translated_text: Pure, peaceful, solitary, consisting of supreme bliss, accessible only to <s>yogins</s> (practitioners),
Difficult to comprehend, difficult to contemplate, supremely beneficial to self and others, pervading, without cause,

children.text: vande kāyaṃ jinānāṃ sukhamasamasamaṃ nirvikalpaikamūrtim || Pik_1 ||
children.translated_text: I salute the body of the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), of incomparable bliss, the single form beyond conceptualization. || 1 ||
From comprehending the meaning of the six million [verses] of the glorious <s>Samājatantra</s> (Assembly Tantra),
I shall expound the <s>Piṇḍīkrama</s> (Stage of Aggregation), which gives rise to the welfare of all beings. || 2 ||
The faults of habitual tendencies of conceptualization, which delude the three worlds,

children.text: samabhivīkṣya tān dhīmān yogatantreṇa śodhayet || Pik_3 ||
children.translated_text: Having carefully examined them, the wise one should purify them through <s>yogatantra</s> (yoga tantra). || 3 ||

body.text: pañca kāmān parityajya tapobhirna ca pīḍayet | Pik_

children.translated_text: One should easily maintain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) in accordance with <s>yogatantra</s> (yoga tantra). || 4 ||

body.translated_text: Abandoning the five desires, one should not torment oneself with austerities;

children.translated_text: Therefore, one abiding in <s>saṃvara</s> (vow), always non-dual, observing the vow,
Should commence the practice of the <s>vajra</s> (diamond) of body, speech, and mind. || 5 ||
In the regions of great forests, adorned with fruits, flowers, and the like,
On a mountain, one should accomplish the accumulation of all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments). || 6 ||
Seated on a soft seat, established in the <s>sattvaparyaṅka</s> (cross-legged posture),
Abiding in the <s>dveṣavajrasamādhi</s> (diamond-of-aversion meditation), one should contemplate the protection of the place. || 7 ||
Sending forth the ten wrathful ones, blazing with flames, terrifying,
Born from the syllable HŪṂ, standing upon suns, in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> (warrior) stance. || 8 ||
At the front of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the ten directions, contemplating thus in sequence,
For the destruction of all obstacles, commanding <s>Sumbha</s>, one should stake [the ground]. || 9 ||

body.text: aṃ sumbha nisumbha hūṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ gṛhṇāpaya gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ ānaya ho bhagavan vidyārāja hūṃ phaṭ |
body.translated_text: AṂ Sumbha Nisumbha HŪṂ, seize, seize HŪṂ, cause to seize, cause to seize HŪṂ, bring forth HO, Blessed <s>Vidyārāja</s> HŪṂ PHAṬ!

children.translated_text: By this wrathful form, having attracted the <s>Vināyakas</s> (obstacle-makers) thus,

children.text: kīlayed vidhivat sarvān prayogeṇa tu buddhimān || Pik_10 ||
children.translated_text: The wise one should stake them all according to the proper method and procedure. || 10 ||
One should visualize the great king <s>Vajrāmṛta</s> as <s>Vajrakīla</s> (diamond stake),
Dark as a blue lotus petal, surrounded by a garland of flames. || 11 ||
Below the navel region, one should visualize a stake-like form,
And above, a wrathful form with three faces and six arms. || 12 ||

children.text: adho vighnagaṇān vīkṣya tān mantraṃ samudāharan |
children.translated_text: Looking down at the hosts of obstacle-makers, reciting this <s>mantra</s>,

children.text: nikhanet vajrakīlaṃ tu vighnadeheṣu niścalam || Pik_13 ||
children.translated_text: One should drive the <s>vajrakīla</s> (diamond stake) firmly into the bodies of the obstacle-makers. || 13 ||

body.text: oṃ gha gha ghātaya ghātaya sarvaduṣṭān phaṭ phaṭ kīlaya kīlaya sarvapāpān phaṭ phaṭ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ vajrakīla vajradhara ājñāpayati sarvavighnānāṃ kāyavākcittavajraṃ kīlaya hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ |
body.translated_text: OṂ GHA GHA, slay, slay all the wicked ones PHAṬ PHAṬ! Stake, stake all sins PHAṬ PHAṬ! HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ! <s>Vajrakīla</s>, <s>Vajradhara</s> commands: stake the body, speech, and mind-vajra of all obstacles HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ!

children.translated_text: One should visualize <s>Sumbharāja</s> (King Sumbha) holding a <s>vajra</s>-hammer in hand,
And <s>vajra</s>-fire spreading forth in all directions;
One should contemplate the wicked ones wailing, being burned here and there. || 14 ||

body.text: daśadik kīlayitvā tu adha ūrdhvamadhiṣya ca |

children.translated_text: One should meditate in ultimate truth on the three realms of existence as devoid of self-nature. || 15 ||
In the absence [of inherent existence], meditation is absent; meditation is truly not meditation.

children.text: iti bhāvo na bhāvaḥ syād bhāvanā nopalabhyate || Pik_16 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, existence is not existence; meditation is not apprehended. || 16 ||

body.translated_text: Having staked the ten directions, and securing below and above,

children.translated_text: Having meditated on the void through this verse, comprising both the moving and the stationary,
By this method of practice, the ground of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom) is attained. || 17 ||
In the midst of the space-element, one should visualize the wind-<s>maṇḍala</s> (circle),
Arisen from the seed-syllables dvi-HŪṂ-YAṂ, endowed with a pair of <s>vajras</s>. || 18 ||
And above that, one should visualize the fire-<s>maṇḍala</s> (circle),
Arisen from the seed-syllables dvi-HŪṂ-RAṂ, marked with a pair of <s>vajras</s>. || 19 ||
And above that, one should visualize the water-<s>maṇḍala</s> (circle),
Arisen from the seed-syllables dvi-HŪṂ-VAṂ, endowed with a pair of <s>vajras</s>. || 20 ||
And above that, one should visualize the earth-<s>maṇḍala</s> (circle),
Arisen from the seed-syllables dvi-HŪṂ-LAṂ, accompanied by a pair of <s>vajras</s>. || 21 ||
Upon the dissolution of the four <s>maṇḍalas</s>, [there arises] the <s>vajra</s>-ground <s>maṇḍala</s>,
And there, arisen from the syllable BHRŪṂ, one should visualize a multi-storied mansion. || 22 ||
Square, with four doors, adorned with four gateways,
Endowed with four strings, beautified by eight pillars. || 23 ||
Decorated with necklaces and half-necklaces, with jewels, <s>vajras</s>, and half-moons,
Inlaid with <s>vajra</s>-gems at the junctions of the door projections. || 24 ||
With a great <s>vajra</s> on the pot-pillar, with birds atop the pinnacles in sequence,
Resplendent with bells and banners, adorned with fly-whisks and the like. || 25 ||
In the central <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should meditate on oneself endowed with the <s>mudrā</s> (seal),
With three faces and six arms, resembling an <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire). || 26 ||
The glorious <s>Vairocana</s>, <s>Ratnasambhava</s>, and <s>Amitābha</s> along with <s>Amoghasiddhi</s> (the lord of action),
Should be contemplated in the eastern and other directions, with three faces and six arms. || 27 ||
The goddesses beginning with <s>Moharatī</s> (Delusion-Passion), with three faces and six arms,
Should be placed beginning from the southeastern direction in due order. || 28 ||
<s>Rūpavajrā</s> (Form-Vajra) and others likewise in the four outer corners;
<s>Sparśavajrā</s> (Touch-Vajra) stands united with <s>Vajrasattva</s>. || 29 ||
On the ledge to the east, one should place <s>Maitreya</s> and <s>Kṣitigarbha</s>;

children.text: vajrapāṇiṃ khagarbhaṃ ca nyased dakṣiṇato vratī || Pik_30 ||
children.translated_text: The practitioner should place <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> and <s>Khagarbha</s> (Ākāśagarbha) to the south. || 30 ||

children.text: lokeśaṃ mañcughoṣaṃ ca paścimāyāṃ nyaset punaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Lokeśa</s> (Avalokiteśvara) and <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> (Mañjuśrī) should be placed in the west;
<s>Sarvāvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> and <s>Samantabhadra</s> in the north. || 31 ||
<s>Yamāntaka</s> at the eastern door, <s>Aparājita</s> at the southern,
<s>Hayagrīva</s> at the western, and <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalin</s> at the northern. || 32 ||
<s>Acala</s>, <s>Ṭakkirāja</s>, <s>Nīladaṇḍa</s>, and <s>Mahābala</s>,
Should be contemplated beginning from the eastern corner in their proper positions. || 33 ||
Below, one should contemplate the great wrathful <s>Sumbharāja</s>,
And <s>Uṣṇīṣacakravartin</s> should be contemplated above. || 34 ||
Having thus meditated with determination on the <s>maṇḍala</s> deities according to the rite,

children.text: punaḥ sampuṭayogena svakāye tān praveśayet || Pik_35 ||
children.translated_text: One should again, through the <s>saṃpuṭa</s> (union) method, cause them to enter one's own body. || 35 ||
Having contemplated the <s>Buddhas</s> situated in the body-wheel thus in their proper places,
One should cause them to enter <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) through the wheel of ultimate truth. || 36 ||
One should dissolve the manifested array; thereby one will assuredly attain <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment).

children.text: asyārtho vajramālāyāṃ vistṛto visphuṭaṃ yathā || Pik_37 ||
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is extensively and clearly [explained] in the <s>Vajramālā</s>. || 37 ||
The mirror[-like wisdom] pertaining to the form-aggregate, the earth-element, the eye-faculty,

children.text: rūpaṃ ca pañcamaṃ yāti krodhamaitreyasaṃyutam || Pik_38 ||
children.translated_text: And form as the fifth — these go to the wrathful one associated with <s>Maitreya</s>. || 38 ||
The equality[-wisdom] of the feeling-aggregate, the water-element, the ear-faculty,
And sound as the fifth — these go accompanied by a pair of wrathful ones. || 39 ||
The discriminating[-wisdom] of the perception-aggregate, the fire-element, the nose-faculty,
And smell as the fifth — these go accompanied by a pair of wrathful ones. || 40 ||
The accomplishing[-wisdom] of the formations-aggregate, the wind-element, the tongue-faculty,
And taste as the fifth — these go accompanied by a pair of wrathful ones. || 41 ||
Conjoined with wrathful ones above and below, and the appearance of <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) itself,
The consciousness-aggregate arises; and consciousness is luminous. || 42 ||
<s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the total void, and <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body) are proclaimed;
For the sake of making firm, one should recite this <s>mantra</s>: || 43 ||

body.translated_text: OṂ! I am of the nature of the <s>vajra</s> (diamond) of the knowledge of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)!

children.translated_text: This is the <s>maṇḍala</s> of ultimate truth, without appearance, without characteristics,
Also called the truth of ultimate reality, the abode of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. || 44 ||
For one who has entered the luminous [state], the arising [from meditation] is shown,
Through the method of <s>mantra</s>-form practice, directed toward the support of the deity. || 45 ||
In the midst of the space-element, one should visualize the sun-<s>maṇḍala</s> (disc),
And above that, the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner should visualize a moon disc. || 46 ||
There, one should visualize an eight-petaled lotus of red color,

children.text: padmopari mahāmantraṃ tryakṣaraṃ bhāvayet punaḥ || Pik_47 ||
children.translated_text: And above the lotus, one should again visualize the great <s>mantra</s> of three syllables. || 47 ||

children.text: mantraṃ padmaṃ tathā sūryaṃ praviṣṭaṃ candramaṇḍale |
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s>, the lotus, and the sun have entered the moon-disc;
One should visualize the moon-disc as filled with <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). || 48 ||
All stationary and moving beings should be contemplated therein,
And for the sake of making firm, one should recite this <s>mantra</s>: || 49 ||

body.translated_text: OṂ! I am of the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of truth)!

children.translated_text: Having thus undertaken this <s>yoga</s> (practice), one should perform the subsequent practice;

children.text: punaśca tryakṣaraṃ yogī candramadhye vicintayet || Pik_50 ||
children.translated_text: And again the <s>yogin</s> should contemplate the three syllables within the moon. || 50 ||
Then, born from the three syllables, white as jasmine and the moon,
Having contemplated <s>Ādinātha</s> (the Primordial Lord), one should commence the supreme <s>yoga</s>. || 51 ||
Through the penetration of <s>Akṣobhya</s>, with three faces and six arms, resplendent,
Brilliant with the radiance of <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire), one should visualize <s>Vajrasattva</s>. || 52 ||

children.text: vajraṃ cakraṃ tathā padmaṃ savyahasteṣu bhāvayet |
children.translated_text: A <s>vajra</s>, a wheel, and a lotus should be visualized in the right hands;

children.text: ghaṇṭāṃ ratnaṃ tathā khaṅgaṃ vāmahasteṣu bhāvayet || Pik_53 ||
children.translated_text: One should visualize a bell, a jewel, and a sword in the left hands. || 53 ||
Then the one who knows the divisions of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so forth should perform the <s>nyāsa</s> (placement),
from <s>Vairocana</s> to <s>Sumbha</s>, through the placement of <s>bījas</s> (seed syllables) in accordance with reality. || 54 ||
The <s>bīja</s> (seed syllable) of <s>Vairocana</s> is the syllable OṂ, white in color,
the knower of <s>mantras</s> should place it on the crown of the head as the essence of <s>rūpaskandha</s> (form aggregate). || 55 ||
The syllable ĀḤ of <s>Amitābha</s>, having the nature of <s>saṃjñāskandha</s> (perception aggregate),
meditating upon it as red in color on the mouth, one attains mastery of speech. || 56 ||
The syllable HŪṂ of <s>Akṣobhya</s>, brilliant like a sapphire,
the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should place it in the heart as the form of <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (consciousness aggregate). || 57 ||
The syllable SVĀ of <s>Ratnanātha</s> (Lord of Jewels), as the form of <s>vedanāskandha</s> (feeling aggregate),
yellow in color, one should place it at the navel as the cause of purifying <s>vedanā</s> (feeling). || 58 ||
The syllable HĀḤ at both feet, as the nature of <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (formations aggregate),
green in color, the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should place it in accordance with the reality of <s>Karmanātha</s> (Lord of Action). || 59 ||
The <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should cause earth and the other elements to enter through <s>Moharati</s> and the other [deities],

children.text: kharatvaṃ dravatā auṣṇyamīraṇatvaṃ ca te kramāt || Pik_60 ||
children.translated_text: hardness, fluidity, heat, and motion respectively, in that order. || 60 ||
Placing the syllable THLĪṂ in the eyes, one should visualize <s>Kṣitigarbha</s>;
placing the syllable OṂ in the ears, one should visualize <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>. || 61 ||

children.text: oṃkāraṃ vinyased ghrāṇe khagarbhaṃ tu vibhāvayet |
children.translated_text: One should place the syllable OṂ in the nose and visualize <s>Khagarbha</s> (Ākāśagarbha);

children.text: oṃkāraṃ rasane dhyātvā lokeśaṃ ca vikalpayet || Pik_62 ||
children.translated_text: meditating on the syllable OṂ on the tongue, one should contemplate <s>Lokeśa</s> (Avalokiteśvara). || 62 ||
Meditating on the syllable HŪṂ in the mind, one should invoke <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> (Mañjuśrī);

children.text: oṃkāraṃ sarvakāye ca dhyātvā viṣkambhiṇaṃ smaret || Pik_63 ||
children.translated_text: meditating on the syllable OṂ throughout the entire body, one should recall <s>Viṣkambhin</s> (Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin). || 63 ||
With the syllable MAIṂ, one should visualize <s>Maitreya</s> stationed at the head;

children.text: bhadraṃ samantato dhyātvā sarvasandhiṣu sannyaset || Pik_64 ||
children.translated_text: meditating on <s>Samantabhadra</s> everywhere, one should place [him] at all the joints. || 64 ||
<s>Yamāntaka</s> on the right arm, <s>Aparājita</s> on the left;

children.text: hayagrīvo mukhe bhāvyo vajre cāmṛtakuṇḍaliḥ || Pik_65 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hayagrīva</s> should be visualized at the mouth, and <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalin</s> at the <s>vajra</s> (secret place). || 65 ||

children.text: acalaṃ dakṣiṇe bhāge vāme ca ṭakkirājakam |
children.translated_text: <s>Acala</s> on the right side, and <s>Ṭakkirāja</s> on the left;

children.text: jānau ca dakṣiṇe cintennīladaṇḍaṃ mahojjavalam || Pik_66 ||
children.translated_text: on the right knee one should contemplate <s>Nīladaṇḍa</s>, greatly blazing. || 66 ||
<s>Mahābala</s> on the left knee, and <s>Uṣṇīṣin</s> (the crowned one) on the crown of the head;
one should contemplate <s>Sumbharāja</s> placed at both soles of the feet. || 67 ||

children.text: nyāsaṃ kṛtvā tato mantrī skandhādīnāṃ yathāvidhi |
children.translated_text: Having thus performed the <s>nyāsa</s> (placement) of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so forth according to the prescribed method,
having attained the <s>kāyamaṇḍala</s> (body maṇḍala), one should commence the <s>mahāyoga</s> (great yoga). || 68 ||
One should visualize at the crown a complete moon disc situated in the center,
and there the syllable OṂ, white in appearance, radiating with five rays of light. || 69 ||
Then, having emanated the goddess through the practice of sovereignty,

children.text: locanāṃ vividhāṃ cintet sarvavyomni prapūritām || Pik_70 ||
children.translated_text: one should visualize <s>Locanā</s> in manifold forms, pervading all of space. || 70 ||
Then, having visualized the <s>kāyavajra</s> (body-vajra) as established pervading space,
in its midst one should contemplate the lord, standing before oneself. || 71 ||
Bearing the thirty-two <s>lakṣaṇas</s> (major marks), adorned with the eighty <s>anuvyañjanas</s> (minor marks),

children.text: prārthayet tu tato mantrī gāthādvayamudāharan || Pik_72 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should then make a supplication, reciting two verses: || 72 ||
"The glorious one who bears the <s>buddhakāya</s> (buddha-body), established in the indestructible three <s>vajras</s>,
may he today bestow upon me the station of empowerment of the <s>kāyavajrin</s> (body-vajra holder)." || 73 ||
"The <s>Buddhas</s> abiding in the ten directions, established in the indestructible three <s>vajras</s>,
may they today bestow upon me the station of empowerment of the <s>kāyavajrin</s> (body-vajra holder)." || 74 ||
One should visualize it as eternal, conjoined with a thousand <s>Locanās</s>,
and having entered that, one should establish [oneself], pervaded by the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). || 75 ||
"That which is the body of all <s>Buddhas</s>, pervaded by the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates),
may mine also become likewise, with the nature of <s>buddhakāya</s> (buddha-body)." || 76 ||

body.translated_text: OṂ — I am of the nature of the body-vajra of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.translated_text: One should visualize in the center of the tongue-lotus the syllable ĀḤ, red in color,

children.text: pāṇḍarākhyāṃ ca sagaṇāṃ saṃspharet vyomapūritām || Pik_77 ||
children.translated_text: and emanate <s>Pāṇḍarā</s> (White Tārā) with her retinue, pervading space. || 77 ||

children.text: vāgvajraṃ ca tathā mantrī vyomāpūrya vyavasthitam |
children.translated_text: Likewise the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner), having established the <s>vāgvajra</s> (speech-vajra) pervading space,

children.text: prārthayet tu tato mantrī gāthādvayamudāharan || Pik_78 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should then make a supplication, reciting two verses: || 78 ||
"The glorious <s>Dharma</s>, the path of speech, established in the indestructible three <s>vajras</s>,
may he today bestow upon me the station of empowerment of the <s>vāgvajrin</s> (speech-vajra holder)." || 79 ||
"The <s>Buddhas</s> abiding in the ten directions, established in the indestructible three <s>vajras</s>,
may they today bestow upon me the station of empowerment of the <s>vāgvajrin</s> (speech-vajra holder)." || 80 ||
United with her own lord, <s>Pāṇḍarā</s> together [with her retinue],
having entered the tongue, one should commence the <s>vāgadhiṣṭhāna</s> (speech empowerment). || 81 ||
"Whatever speech <s>Vajradharma</s> possesses, perfect in expression,

children.text: mamāpi tādṛśī vācā bhaved dharmadharopamā || Pik_82 ||
children.translated_text: may my speech also become likewise, equal to a holder of the <s>Dharma</s>." || 82 ||

body.translated_text: OṂ — I am of the nature of the speech-vajra of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.translated_text: The <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) having placed in the heart a brilliantly shining moon disc,
therein the syllable HŪṂ, sapphire-like, with five rays. || 83 ||

children.text: tato niścārayed devīṃ māmakīṃ sagaṇāṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Then one should emanate the goddess <s>Māmakī</s> with her retinue,

children.text: cittavajraṃ tathā dhyātvā prārthayeta yathā puraḥ || Pik_84 ||
children.translated_text: and likewise having meditated on the <s>cittavajra</s> (mind-vajra), one should make a supplication as before: || 84 ||
"The glorious holder of the <s>cittavajra</s> (mind-vajra), established in the indestructible three <s>vajras</s>,
may he today bestow upon me the station of empowerment of the <s>cittavajrin</s> (mind-vajra holder)." || 84 ||
"The <s>Buddhas</s> abiding in the ten directions, established in the indestructible three <s>vajras</s>,
may they today bestow upon me the station of empowerment of the <s>cittavajrin</s> (mind-vajra holder)." || 84 ||
United with the <s>cittavajra</s> (mind-vajra), having entered it into the heart,
with the entire array of <s>Māmakī</s>, one should commence the <s>cittādhiṣṭhāna</s> (mind empowerment). || 87 ||

body.text:

resembling a ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>), three-eyed, with faces of red, black, and white. (Pik 165)
With a terrifying mouth, great belly, crowned by <s>Amitābha</s>,
in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> posture, heroic, enveloped in a mass of sparks. (Pik 166)

children.text: padmaṃ khaṅgaṃ ca musalaṃ savyahasteṣu bhāvayet |
children.translated_text: A lotus, sword, and pestle (<s>musala</s>) one should visualize in the right hands;

children.text: ghaṇṭāṃ sagarvaparaśuṃ pāśaṃ savyetareṣu ca || Pik_167 ||
children.translated_text: a bell, an axe with pride, and a noose in the left [hands]. (Pik 167)
Having mounted the lotus-sun, having surveyed the ten directions,

children.text: vidhnasantrāsanaṃ kṛtvā vāruṇyāṃ diśi tiṣṭhati || Pik_168 ||
children.translated_text: having terrified the obstacles, he stands in the western direction. (Pik 168)
Born from the mantra of <s>Vighnāntakṛt</s> (Destroyer of Obstacles), crowned with the sound of a drum (<s>dundubhi</s>),
dark as a blue lotus petal — one should emanate [him] with <s>Amṛta</s> (nectar) earrings. (Pik 169)
With faces of blue, red, and white, with the play of a terrifying mouth,
great-bellied, three-eyed, adorned with red flames. (Pik 170)

children.text: viśvavajraṃ tathā vakraṃ musalaṃ cāpi savyataḥ |
children.translated_text: A <s>viśvavajra</s> (crossed thunderbolt), a hook (<s>vakra</s>), and a pestle in the right [hands];

children.text: dhārayaṃstarjanīpāśaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ paraśuṃ ca vāmataḥ || Pik_171 ||
children.translated_text: bearing a threatening-finger noose, a bell, and an axe in the left. (Pik 171)
Having terrified the obstacles, in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> posture,

children.text: padmasūryaṃ samāruhya kauberyāṃ diśi tiṣṭhati || Pik_172 ||
children.translated_text: having mounted the lotus-sun, he stands in the direction of <s>Kubera</s> (north). (Pik 172)
One should then emanate <s>Acala</s> (the Immovable), arisen from the syllables of his own mantra,
radiant as an indigo sapphire, three-eyed, crowned by <s>Śrī Vairocana</s>. (Pik 173)
With a face terrifying with fangs, with faces of black, red, and white,
with terrible roaring laughter, great-bellied, of immense power. (Pik 174)

children.text: khaṅkaṃ vajraṃ tathā cakraṃ savyahasteṣu dhārayet |
children.translated_text: A sword, <s>vajra</s>, and discus (<s>cakra</s>) he should hold in the right hands;

children.text: tarjanīṃ cāpi paraśuṃ pāśaṃ vāmeṣu pāṇiṣu || Pik_178 ||
children.translated_text: a threatening finger, an axe, and a noose in the left hands. (Pik 178)
Having slain the obstacles such as fever, in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> posture,

children.text: padmasūryaṃ samāruhya vahnisthāne sa tiṣṭhati || Pik_176 ||
children.translated_text: having mounted the lotus-sun, he stands in the place of fire (southeast). (Pik 176)
The practitioner should emanate <s>Ṭakkirāja</s>, arisen from the syllables of his own mantra,
radiant as an indigo sapphire, heroic, crowned by <s>Ratnasambhava</s>. (Pik 177)

children.text: dadhānaṃ vajraṃ hūṃkāramudrāṃ paṇidvayena tu || Pik_178 ||
children.translated_text: bearing a <s>vajra</s> with the <s>hūṃkāra-mudrā</s> (gesture of HŪṂ) in both hands. (Pik 178)

body.translated_text: With faces of black, red, and white, great-bellied, terrifying,

children.text: vajraṃ khaḍgaṃ ca savyābhyāṃ vāmataḥ pāśamaṅkuśam |
children.translated_text: A <s>vajra</s> and sword in the right [hands]; a noose and goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>) in the left;
in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> [posture], standing on the sun, in the southwest, the destroyer of obstacles. (Pik 179)
The practitioner should emanate <s>Nīladaṇḍa</s> (Blue Staff), arisen from the syllables of his own mantra,
resembling a blue cloud, three-eyed, crowned by <s>Amitābha</s>. (Pik 180)
With faces of blue, red, and white, great-bellied, fearsome,

children.text: daṇḍaṃ khaṅgaṃ tathā savyahasteṣu dhārayan || Pik_181 ||
children.translated_text: bearing a staff and sword in the right hands. (Pik 181)

children.text: hṛdeśe tarjanīpāśaṃ padmaṃ paraśuṃ ca vāmataḥ |
children.translated_text: At the heart, a threatening-finger noose; a lotus and axe in the left;
having slain the fear of calamities, standing in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> posture. (Pik 182)
Having mounted the lotus-sun, he stands in the northwest direction.
Arisen from the syllables of his own mantra, crowned with the sound of a drum. (Pik 183)
The <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should emanate [him] of great power, radiant as a blue lotus petal,
with faces of black, red, and white, three-eyed, with a terrifying <s>Bhairava</s>-like roar. (Pik 184)
All limbs adorned with serpents, great-bellied, fearsome,

children.text: daṇḍaṃ khaḍgaṃ tathā cakraṃ savyahasteṣu dhārayan || Pik_185 ||
children.translated_text: bearing a staff, sword, and discus in the right hands. (Pik 185)

children.text: hṛddeśe tarjanīpāśaṃ padmaṃ paraśuṃ ca vāmataḥ |
children.translated_text: At the heart, a threatening-finger noose; a lotus and axe in the left;
the destroyer of fears from <s>ḍākinīs</s> and others, in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> posture. (Pik 186)
Having mounted the lotus-sun, he stands in the northeast (<s>Aiśāna</s>) direction.
One should emanate <s>Uṣṇīṣacakrin</s> (Crown-Wheel), arisen from the syllables of his own mantra. (Pik 187)
Dark as the sky, terrifying, with <s>Akṣobhya</s> as the crest,

children.text: kṛṣṇaraktasitāsyaṃ ca tryakṣaṃ lambodaraṃ vibhum || Pik_188 ||
children.translated_text: with faces of black, red, and white, three-eyed, pot-bellied, all-pervading. (Pik 188)
Bearing the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown) on his head with both right and left hands;

children.text: vajraṃ padmaṃ ca savyābhyāṃ tarjanīkhaḍgamanyataḥ || Pik_189 ||
children.translated_text: a <s>vajra</s> and lotus in the right [hands]; a threatening finger and sword in the other. (Pik 189)
The destroyer of all calamities, rising in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> posture,

children.text: padmasūryaṃ samāruhya brahmasthāne sa tiṣṭhati || Pik_190 ||
children.translated_text: having mounted the lotus-sun, he stands in the place of <s>Brahmā</s> (zenith). (Pik 190)
The practitioner should emanate <s>Sumbharāja</s>, arisen from the syllables of his own mantra,
brilliantly radiant as the sky, three-eyed, with faces of black, red, and white. (Pik 191)
Great-bellied, with a terrifying mouth, with <s>Akṣobhya</s> as the crest,

children.text: vajraṃ cakraṃ tathā ratnaṃ savyahasteṣu dhārayan || Pik_192 ||
children.translated_text: bearing a <s>vajra</s>, discus, and jewel in the right hands. (Pik 192)
At the heart, a threatening-finger noose; a lotus and sword in the left;
all poisons — <s>kālakūṭa</s> and others, both stationary and mobile — (Pik 193)

children.text: hatvā vināyakān sarvān śāntiṃ kṛtvā tu sarvataḥ |
children.translated_text: having slain all the <s>Vināyakas</s> (obstacle-beings), having made peace everywhere,
having accomplished complete authority, standing in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> posture,

children.text: padmasūryaṃ samāruhya bhuvo 'dhastāt sa tiṣṭhati || Pik_194 ||
children.translated_text: having mounted the lotus-sun, he stands beneath the earth. (Pik 194)
Having released the entire <s>maṇḍala</s> consisting of thirty-two deities,
having become positioned at the center of the wheel, one should then begin the subtle yoga (<s>sūkṣmayoga</s>). (Pik 194)
One should contemplate a mustard seed at the tip of the nose; in the mustard seed, [visualize] the entire moving and unmoving [universe].
One should meditate on the delightful seat of knowledge (<s>jñānapada</s>), the secret one, established by wisdom. (Pik 196)

children.text: sthiraṃ tu sphārayed ratnamasthiraṃ naiva sphārayet |
children.translated_text: One should expand the stable jewel; the unstable one should not be expanded.
One should expand with excellent clouds, radiant like the flame of a <s>Buddha</s>. (Pik 197)

children.text: bhikṣāśinā na japtapyaṃ na ca bhaikṣarato bhavet |
children.translated_text: One who eats alms-food should not recite [the mantra]; nor should one live on begging [alone].
One should recite the mantra with unbroken limbs — it fulfills all desires and enjoyments. (Pik 198)

body.text:
uccārya saṃsphared vajraṃ samāptau saṃhāramādiśet |
idaṃ tat sarvabuddhānāṃ japoktaṃ paramārthataḥ || Pik_iti | Pik_ 199 ||
body.translated_text: Having uttered [the mantra], one should touch the <s>vajra</s>; at the conclusion, one should indicate the dissolution. This is the recitation proclaimed by all the <s>Buddhas</s> in the ultimate sense. (Pik 199)

children.translated_text: The subtle yoga recitation, having divided it in two according to one's preference,

children.text: ātmānaṃ ca punarmantrī tathatāyāṃ praveśayet || Pik_200 ||
children.translated_text: the practitioner should again enter himself into <s>tathatā</s> (suchness/reality-as-it-is). (Pik 200)
The four goddesses stationed in the <s>maṇḍala</s>, not seeing their lord,
awaken [him to] great bliss (<s>mahāsukha</s>) with four verses as follows: (Pik 201)

children.text: tvaṃ vajrasattva bhuvaneśvara sattvadhāto trāyāhi māṃ ratinojñamahārthakāmaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Vajrasattva</s>, lord of worlds, essence of beings, protect me with pleasures of great purpose and delight!

children.text: kāmāhi māṃ janaka sattvamahāgrabandho yadīcchase jīvatu mahya nātha || Pik_202 ||
children.translated_text: Love me, O progenitor, great bond of beings! If you wish [me] to live, O my lord!' (Pik 202)
'O <s>Vajrakāya</s> (Vajra-body), foremost wheel beloved of many beings, you who perceive the ultimate benefit of Buddha-purpose and enlightenment,

children.text: rāgeṇa rāgasamayāṃ mama kāmayasva yadīcchase jīvatu mahya nātha || Pik_203 ||
children.translated_text: love me with passion, [she] who is the occasion of passion! If you wish [me] to live, O my lord!' (Pik 203)

children.text: tvaṃ vajravāca sakalasya hitānukampī lokārthakāryakaraṇe sada sampravṛttaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Vajravāca</s> (Vajra-speech), compassionate for the welfare of all, ever engaged in accomplishing deeds for the benefit of the world,

children.text: kāmāhi māṃ sugatacarya samantabhadra yadīcchase jīvatu mahya nātha || Pik_204 ||
children.translated_text: love me, O <s>Samantabhadra</s>, practitioner of the <s>Sugata</s>'s path! If you wish [me] to live, O my lord!' (Pik 204)

children.text: tvaṃ vajrakāma samayāgra mahāhitārtha saṃbuddhavaṃśatilakaḥ samatānukampī |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Vajrakāma</s> (Vajra-desire), foremost of pledges, of great beneficent purpose, ornament of the lineage of fully awakened ones, compassionate with equanimity,

children.text: kāmāhi mām guṇanidhiṃ bahuratnabhūtāṃ yadīcchase jīvatu mahya nātha || Pik_205 ||
children.translated_text: love me, a treasury of virtues, rich with many jewels! If you wish [me] to live, O my lord!' (Pik 205)
The lord, thus aroused by the proclamation of true virtues,
the <s>Tathāgatas</s> praise him with the nature of <s>Akṣobhya</s> and others: (Pik 206)
'O <s>Akṣobhya</s>-<s>Vajra</s>, great knowledge, <s>Vajradhātu</s> (Vajra-realm), great wisdom!

children.text: trimaṇḍala trivajrāgra bhāṣa guhyaṃ namo 'stu te || Pik_207 ||
children.translated_text: Foremost of three <s>maṇḍalas</s> and three <s>vajras</s>, speak the secret! Homage to you!' (Pik 207)
'O <s>Vairocana</s>, greatly pure, <s>Vajraśānta</s> (Vajra-peace), great delight!

children.text: prakṛtiprabhāsvarān dharmān deśa vajra namo 'stu te || Pik_208 ||
children.translated_text: Teach the <s>dharmas</s> that are by nature luminous (<s>prabhāsvara</s>), O <s>Vajra</s>! Homage to you!' (Pik 208)
'O <s>Ratnarāja</s> (Jewel-king), profoundly deep, sky-<s>vajra</s>, immaculate as space,

children.text: svabhāvaśuddha nirlepa bhāṣa guhyaṃ namo 'stu te || Pik_209 ||
children.translated_text: pure by nature, unstained — speak the secret! Homage to you!' (Pik 209)
'O great king <s>Vajrāmita</s> (Immeasurable Vajra), free from conceptual elaboration, sky-<s>vajra</s> holder,

children.text: rājapāramitāprāpta bhāṣa vajra namo 'stu te || Pik_210 ||
children.translated_text: who has attained the perfection of sovereignty — speak, O <s>Vajra</s>! Homage to you!' (Pik 210)
'O <s>Amoghavajra</s> (Infallible Vajra), fully awakened, fulfiller of all hopes,
born of pure nature — O <s>Vajrasattva</s>, homage to you!' (Pik 211)

children.text: nutvātha buddhaiaranurāgya cakram prakāśya guhyaṃ paramaṃ yathāyatham |
children.translated_text: Then, having bowed to the <s>Buddhas</s> with devotion, having revealed the supreme secret wheel as appropriate,

children.text: svakāyacakre viniveśya cakram mahāsukhastiṣṭhati nātha ekaḥ || Pik_212 ||
children.translated_text: having placed the wheel in his own body-wheel, the lord alone abides in great bliss (<s>mahāsukha</s>). (Pik 212)

body.text:
evaṃ caturyogakarastu yogī hūṃkāragarbhaṃ pravicintya lokam |
dṛṣṭvā japat tadbhavavajrasattvaṃ vyutthāya taddhīrvicared yathāvad || iti | Pik_213 ||
body.translated_text: Thus the yogin, practitioner of the four yogas, having contemplated the world as the womb of HŪṂ, having seen and recited [the mantra of] <s>Vajrasattva</s> born therefrom, having arisen, one of firm intelligence should conduct [oneself] properly. (Pik 213)

children.translated_text: When the practitioner, relying on <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), becomes of dried-up form,
he should contemplate this yoga, which delights body, speech, and mind. (Pik 214)
Having ascended a span (<s>vitasti</s>), the <s>maṇḍala</s> visualization at the crown of the head;
having meditated on OṂ located there, the descent of the five nectars (<s>pañcāmṛta</s>). (Pik 215)
By this <s>vajra</s>-yoga, one becomes radiant in an instant;
one obtains well-being of body, speech, and mind — there is no doubt about this. (Pik 216)
Thus, through repeated practice, the practitioner should purify and awaken as follows:

children.text: hṛtkaṇṭhaṃ caiva saṃśodhyaṃ prīṇayecca tathāgatān || Pik_217 ||
children.translated_text: One should purify the heart and throat, and please the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. || 217 ||

children.text: hūṃkāreṇa ca saṃśodhya āḥkāreṇa tu bodhayet |
children.translated_text: Having purified with the syllable HŪṂ, one should awaken with the syllable ĀḤ;
One should cause it to blaze, pervaded by the syllable OṂ — this is the purification of food. || 218 ||
First, one should visualize a conch at the throat, and therein, born from the syllable HRĪḤ,
One should contemplate an eight-petaled lotus, with the syllable HŪṂ upon the pericarp. || 219 ||
One should visualize a great <s>vajra</s> born from the syllable HŪṂ, with five prongs,
And at the tip of the central prong, one should contemplate the syllable OṂ — this is the purification of the throat. || 220 ||

children.text: meghanādaṃ hṛdi dhyātvā triśikhāgniṃ tataḥ spharet |
children.translated_text: Having meditated on thunder-sound in the heart, one should then emit a three-pointed flame;

children.text: tatrāhāraṃ ca juhuyād homamādhyātmikaṃ tvidam || Pik_221 ||
children.translated_text: Therein one should offer food as oblation — this is the inner <s>homa</s> (fire ritual). || 221 ||

children.text: vāyavyaṃ dīpayed agniṃ vāruṇaṃ pacate tu saḥ |
children.translated_text: The wind kindles the fire, and the water cooks;

children.text: māhendramaṇḍalaṃ sthānaṃ yatra sañcarate haviḥ || Pik_222 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Mahendra</s> (great Indra) is the place where the oblation circulates. || 222 ||

children.text: annaṃ pānaṃ ca yat kiñcit tat sarvaṃ vāruṇena tu |
children.translated_text: Whatever food and drink there may be, all of that, through the water [element],
As nourishment through the mouth-lotus, one should cause it to enter the heart-lotus. || 223 ||
Having then reached the navel-lotus, through the method of <s>saṃpuṭīkaraṇa</s> (enclosure),

children.text: gudapadmād vinirgatya bhaśmāntaṃ ca vinirdiśet || Pik_224 ||
children.translated_text: Emerging from the anus-lotus, one should declare it to end as ash. || 224 ||

body.text:
na jarā nāpi rogaśca na mṛtyurna viṣādikam |
nākālamaraṇaṃ tasya sarvopadravanāśanam || Pik_iti | Pik_ 225 ||
body.translated_text: There is no old age, no disease, no death, no poison and the like, no untimely death for that one — it destroys all calamities. || 225 ||

children.translated_text: Having churned the ocean of the <s>Samāja</s> (Assembly) with the supreme churning rod of the glorious <s>Vajramālā</s>,

children.text: yat sādanāṅgāmṛtamāpi tena lokaḥ samasto 'maratāmupaitu || Pik_226 ||
children.translated_text: By that nectar of the limbs of practice thus obtained, may the entire world attain immortality! || 226 ||

body.translated_text: || The <s>Piṇḍīkramasādhana</s> (Practice of the Stage of Aggregation) is complete. ||
| This is the composition of the venerable <s>Ācārya Śrī Nāgārjunapāda</s>. |
